$schema_note: Release notes authored here (ADR-0002), one entry per release, newest first; rendered to /docs/reference/changelog/, its twin and /docs/changelog.json by src/lib/docs/generated/changelog.ts. Each item is one sentence of inline markdown ending with a period; `breaking: true` marks a change that can make working code or statements fail; `pages` lists the page ids (with an optional #anchor) that document it, linked once published. Facts come from upstream's release notes (public/releases.json) and are checked against the binary named in cli.json `recorded_with` where the CLI can show them. The verified engine version (_data/engine.json) must be an entry or an entry's `previous`: every twin links #since-<verified>.
policy: relate is pre-1.0. Its releases follow semantic versioning, under which anything can change in a 0.x release, a patch release included: 0.16.1 removed the `apoc.coll.sort` spelling and replaced the C ABI with an incompatible typed one.

A change that can make working code or statements fail is marked **Breaking** in the entry of the release that ships it, under Changed or Removed, with its replacement when there is one. A feature that still works but is to be removed is listed under Deprecated in the release that deprecates it.

releases.summary: The first stable release, and the first published to PyPI (`relate-db`), npm (`@relate/relate`, `@relate/relate-wasm`) and crates.io (`relate`). The Rust crate's change-data-capture methods are removed, and messages no longer cite internal design records.

added.text: The clients are on their registries at the release's version: `pip install relate-db`, `npm install @relate/relate` (with its platform package) and `@relate/relate-wasm`, and `cargo add relate`. The npm packages carry npm provenance and the PyPI files trusted-publishing attestations. The Java jars stay release downloads.

changed.text: Messages no longer end with an upstream design-record reference: for example `pull writes into an empty database only` and `serve: opened the store read-only — no writer lease …`, where 0.1.3 added `(ADR-0158)` and `(ADR-0306)`.

`relate upgrade` reads only the release list it names, with no fallback host, and its error reads `could not read the release list: GET <url>: <reason>; reinstall manually instead: curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash`; `install.sh` resolves the latest release from `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json` too.
Opening an `s3://` URI reports that object storage belongs to the clients that embed relate.

removed.text: The Rust crate's change-data-capture methods, `register_cdc_slot`, `ack_cdc_slot`, `drop_cdc_slot`, `cdc_slots`, `cdc_records_after`, `set_apply_only` and `apply_only`, and the `CdcSlot` type. A checkpoint no longer keeps WAL segments for a slot, and a `cdc/slots.json` file is ignored. `apply_replicated` stays.

releases.summary: Element ids carry the shorter `rl-id` segment, the Parquet codec always writes typed columns, errors report the class of the stage that raised them, and every spelling of a shortest-path query takes the dedicated shortest-route engine.

added.text: The procedure `dbms.listCapabilities()` answers with four rows on what this engine can do: `cypher.version`, `fulltext.index`, `vector.index` and `pattern.engine`.

Notification `03C94`, `Relate.Notification.Statement.LabelDisjunctionScan`, on an equality on a property of a label disjunction, such as `(p:Model OR p:Source) AND p.id = 1`, that no range index on each label serves; with those indexes the plan's `NodeByLabelSeek` looks the value up once per label.

changed.text: `elementId()` writes the namespace segment as `rl-id`: the first node of the default database is `4:rl-id:n0` and its first relationship `5:rl-id:r0`, where 0.1.2 returned `4:relate-neo4j:n0` and `5:relate-neo4j:r0`. An id in the old spelling matches no entity.

The `parquet` codec always writes a typed column per shared property key (format version `5`, `6` with an ontology), and `--snapshot-format parquet-wide` is no longer a value: it fails with `unknown snapshot format 'parquet-wide'`. A store written at format version `3` or `4` opens, and its next checkpoint rewrites every data file.
`SHOW INDEXES` lists two lookup indexes on every store, `index_460996c0` on node labels and `index_1b9dcc97` on relationship types; they can't be dropped and the schema copy leaves them out.

`SHOW PROCEDURES` lists 31 rows, where 0.1.2 listed 88: the catalog entries for change data capture, server configuration and connections, clustering and routing, fleet management, usage statistics, index resampling and the vector-property setters are gone. A `CALL` to one of them still fails with `ProcedureNotFound`.

Errors report the class of the stage that raised them: a rejection the statement text decides is a `syntax` error (several `USE` targets in one statement included), a function argument out of its domain at run time, such as `range()` with a step of 0, has the kind `argument` and the Bolt code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ArgumentError`, a `DELETE` of a node with relationships begins `ConstraintVerificationFailed: DeleteConnectedNode:`, and a float `SKIP` or `LIMIT` adds `, got FLOAT` to its message.
The Go and Swift clients type a notification's severity and category (`Severity`, `Category`) and refuse a value outside them; 0.1.2 used plain strings.
The Node.js client's platform packages are `@relate/relate-<platform>-<arch>`, such as `@relate/relate-darwin-arm64`.
The Python client's `element_id` values are always strings; a graph value from the `system` namespace raises `RuntimeError` instead of carrying `None`.

Every spelling of a shortest-path query, the `shortestPath()` expression, `SHORTEST k` selectors and quantified relationships included, takes the dedicated shortest-route engine, and a `MATCH` with OR'd labels and a key predicate is served as a union of per-label seeks.

releases.summary: Element ids carry the database's name, and a shortest path between two endpoints matched by property maps is searched from both ends.

changed.text: `elementId()` names the database: the first node of the default database is `4:relate-neo4j:n0` and its first relationship `5:relate-neo4j:r0`, where 0.1.1 returned `4:relate:n0` and `5:relate:r0`, and the clients, JSON output and Bolt carry the same strings.
A `shortestPath` whose two endpoints are matched by property maps looks up both endpoints and searches from both ends at once.
Opening a store whose write-ahead log replays nothing no longer rebuilds its indexes.
`relate upgrade` no longer prints the notice of the rename after its status line.

releases.summary: Full-text search reads the index's query syntax and ranks by BM25, and the Parquet codec can store each promoted property in a column of its own.

added.text: `--snapshot-format parquet-wide`, on a query run and on `relate serve`, which gains the flag: the Parquet codec writes one typed column per promoted property key, and from the store's next checkpoint on every later open keeps it wide.
Full-text search pages with `SKIP` and `OFFSET`, and `WITH ANALYZER` is evaluated per row, English stemming included.

changed.text: Full-text search passes the query string to the index's query syntax, so `AND` and `NOT` are operators while a lowercase `and` stays a term, and it ranks hits by BM25 scores, so a hit's `score` and the order of hits can differ from 0.1.0.
The Java client's `QueryType`, `Namespace`, `Severity` and `Category` are enums instead of strings, and `PlanActual` carries the whole plan shape.
POINT indexes seek radius and bounding-box queries through an R*-tree.
The variable-shadowing notification also looks inside the bodies of `EXISTS`, `COUNT` and `COLLECT` subqueries.

fixed.text: `round()` on a decimal, the sort order of temporal values, and the type of a nested list whose elements have mixed types.
A list value at a `WHERE` or `FILTER` position is coerced to a predicate.
`FINISH` is accepted after a catalog command that returns rows, and a schema command runs only as a statement of its own.

releases.summary: The first release published as relate, which restarts the version line at 0.1.0 after cypherlite's 0.16.1: the release assets are `relate-<os>-<arch>` and `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz`, and the signer and the signature namespace are `relate-release`, with the same key.

added.text: Every machine-readable result carries per-phase timings and the plan cache's outcome: `--mode envelope` and `--mode json` add a `timings` object and `planCache`, `--mode jsonl` ends each statement with a line holding both, `--mode toon` ends with `timings:` and `planCache:` entries, the envelope of MCP and the WebAssembly build adds `lex_parse_ms`, `rewrite_ms`, `lower_ms`, `result_generation_ms` and `plan_cache`, and the Rust crate's `QueryResult` adds the same four timings and `plan_cache()`; the C ABI and the other clients expose none of them yet.
The `FOR` clause runs without a preview gate.

changed.text: `--mode json` prints an object for every statement, `{"data": [...], "planCache": ..., "timings": {...}}`, where 0.16.1 printed a bare array for a result the row cap did not cut.
`--mode jsonl` prints one more line per statement, its timings, so a statement with no rows prints that one line instead of nothing.

`relate clone` refuses a `markdown` store as the source of a `.rl` bundle unless `--to-snapshot-format` names `parquet` or `json`, with `Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored`.

Usage metrics are written to a local spool at exit and sent by the next run, so an exit never waits on the network, and `RELATE_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_MS` is removed; `relate telemetry off` deletes the spool.

fixed.text: `coll.max()` returns null when the list holds a null, as Neo4j does.
`toString()` of a path and an index into a null string return what Neo4j returns.
A count-style aggregate over a repeated node variable counts only self-loops.
In the Swift client, `transaction(_:)` rolls back when `commit()` throws.

releases.summary: The last release published under the name cypherlite: its release assets carry that name, and a successful `cypherlite upgrade` ends with a notice of the rename and the relate install command.

changed.text: The C ABI is the typed ABI v2: `relate_abi_version()` returns 2, values are read through typed accessors instead of JSON strings, parameters are passed through a typed builder instead of a JSON string, and an error arrives as one object with `code`, `gql_status`, `stage`, `retryable` and `message`.
The Python binding and the Java, JavaScript, Go and Swift clients use the typed ABI v2.
The typed parameter builder is bounded: at most 100,000 entries per container, 4 KiB per name, and 16 MiB in all.
A bookmark carries the engine's commit sequence, through the C ABI, Python and Bolt.
An error of the internal class crosses the C ABI with a generic message; the internal detail stays inside the engine.
A non-boolean value where Cypher requires a boolean, such as a quantifier's `WHERE` or an operand of `AND`, `OR` or `XOR`, fails with `InvalidArgumentType` instead of a generic syntax error.

A clause that reads an entity it creates fails with `Entity, '<name>', cannot be created and referenced in the same clause`, and a `CREATE` or `MERGE` whose node is bound to null fails instead of creating a new node.
An administration command with a `USE` clause that names a graph other than `system` fails with `UseClauseWithAdministrationCommand`.

removed.text: The `apoc.coll.sort` spelling: a call fails as an unknown function, `UnknownFunction: unknown function apoc.coll.sort()`, and `coll.sort` is the replacement.

fixed.text: A frontier search that exhausts its re-arrival budget falls back to the plain walk instead of dropping endpoints, which could make `count(DISTINCT n)` return 0 on a dense clique.
`push` keeps a node's secondary labels and merges on its keyed label, so an update no longer creates a second node.
